Singularity AIDRProduct Catalog 2026End-to-end lifecycle

The entire AI agent security lifecycle, in one platform

Singularity AIDR follows AI agents and AI chat tools from discovery to proof: it finds what exists, measures the risk, protects data, controls actions, inspects output, manages human approval and response, and proves the outcome. Simulation and coverage results feed back into policy, and a governance layer spans every stage.

Why Singularity AIDR?

Local-first processing

Detection and decisions happen on the device; agents and Browser Guard are protected with no account or network.

Reversible masking

The AI keeps its context; the original value comes back only on the user's screen.

Turkish-specific detection

T.C. Kimlik and IBAN by checksum; Turkish phones, addresses, labels and classification marks.

One engine for agents and chat

The same TR/EN rules run in the browser, in agent DLP and on the command line.

Auditable decisions

Rules are readable data, and a person, not the agent, gives approval.

Your choice of deployment

Cloud, on-premises or air-gapped; local protection continues even if a licence lapses.

Highlight · Control actions 47

Toxic flow (lethal trifecta) and attack-chain detection

If one session lets an agent touch private data, read untrusted content and reach an external channel, everything needed to exfiltrate data is in place. AIDR tracks these three conditions across the session and holds the step that would complete the chain for a person's approval, or blocks it at the strictest setting. Sending data out after a secret was read, and destructive commands after untrusted content, are caught as well.

What reaches the console?

Only CVE IDs, severities, component and version, rule IDs and digests. Target addresses, file paths, matched text and credentials stay on the device. An unreachable target is never reported as clean.

What you getYou know about vulnerable services and risky plugins before your agents use them.

Protect data

While AI is in use, sensitive data is masked or stopped before it reaches a model.

What the user types
Draft a refund letter to Mrs. Ayşe Yılmaz. TCKN 10000000146, IBAN TR33 0006 1005 1978 6457 8413 26, email ayse.yilmaz@example.com, key AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE
What the site receives
Draft a refund letter to Mrs. [PERSON_1]. TCKN [TCKN_1], IBAN [IBAN_1], email [EMAIL_1], key [SECRET_1]
On the user's screen
Dear Ayşe Yılmaz, your refund goes to TR33 0006 1005 1978 6457 8413 26; we will write to ayse.yilmaz@example.com. Rotate [SECRET_1].

Masking and restore were produced with Browser Guard's default settings on this example; the answer is illustrative. The key is never shown again.

AIDR Browser Guard · ChatGPT · Gemini · Claude · Copilot · Perplexity · DeepSeek · Mistral · Grok · Chrome, Edge, Firefox

  1. 09Reversible masking — a sensitive value becomes a placeholder such as [EMAIL_1] before sending.
  2. 10Restore on the user's screen only — the answer shows the original value; the site never sees it.

AI safety · risks from the agent's own behaviour

  1. 50Runaway and budget guardrails — loops, failure streaks, call spikes or optional budgets pause the session.
  2. 51Reward hacking and sabotage — skipping tests or hooks, removing asserts, disabling CI, force-push need approval.
  3. 52Autonomy-escalation blocking — agents launching agents in skip-permissions, YOLO or full-auto mode are blocked.
  4. 53Irreversible actions — DB drops, cloud deletions, terraform destroy, publishing and messaging need approval.
  5. 54Safe model loading — pickle/torch.load, trust_remote_code and untrusted model downloads are held or blocked.
  6. 55Secure-code guardrails — TLS off, SQL concatenation, eval on input, weak crypto: warned as written; hold optional.
  7. 56Agent environment posture — permission bypass, hooks off, no sandbox, root, Docker socket; each with a fix.
  8. 57Jailbreak and content-safety policy — conservative patterns warn on or block jailbreaks and prohibited requests.
  9. 58Human-oversight metrics — approval ratio, decision time and fast-approval prompts on the governance scorecard.

Inspect output

What the agent reads back is inspected before it can steer the next step.

  1. 59Tool-output scanning — finds leaked keys, prompt-injection payloads and system-prompt leaks.
  2. 60Quarantine notice — a risky result is replaced before the model sees it; outbound messages too.
  3. 61MCP output inspection — the MCP Gateway scans each result in full before the model gets it.
  4. 62Data and context poisoning protection — instruction files, content read, MCP tool descriptions and memory writes are guarded.

Highlight · OWASP LLM04 and Agentic ASI06

Data and context poisoning protection

  • Instruction and memory files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .cursorrules, MCP and agent settings) are guarded at runtime: writes need approval; invisible Unicode and hidden instructions are blocked.
  • Content the agent reads (files, fetched pages, tool output) is scanned: hidden payloads are kept from the model, and suspicious directives come with a warning to it.
  • MCP tool poisoning and rug pulls: tool descriptions are scanned for hidden instructions; the approved tool list is pinned and any later change is blocked until an operator re-approves.
  • Memory and vector-store writes are scanned before they are stored; with package checks on, invented package names (slopsquatting) are stopped.

What you getInstructions and leaked keys in tool results cannot steer the model.

Frameworks mapped

OWASP LLM Top 10 (2025)OWASP Agentic Top 10 (2026)MITRE ATLASNIST AI RMFISO/IEC 42001EU AI ActKVKKGDPR

Designed to support KVKK and GDPR obligations. Reports and mappings support accountability work; they are not a compliance attestation on their own. Coverage is stated per item: for example, inter-agent communication and cascading failures (OWASP Agentic ASI07, ASI08) are not covered.

What you getAI use is owned, approved and mapped to the frameworks you report against.
